answer: Rate-limited weight accrual resists sybils: an identity's influence can rise by only a small capped amount each epoch and only from verified work, so weight climbs a slow trellis rather than arriving full-grown. Reaching a heavy seat takes many epochs of sustained real contribution; a day-one swarm, however large, starts near zero and accrues no faster than the per-epoch cap times its genuine output. A sudden gale of fresh fakes buys no instant influence, for the umber patina of standing is earned only over time.
